# Results — Study 370 (Zero-DTE Options & the SPX tape)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — that the
**0DTE-options boom** (same-day SPX/SPY options going *daily* in 2022) made the intraday tape
more **mean-reverting / more pinned** — tested on **labelled daily proxies**, because there is
no free intraday SPX option tape. From daily SPY OHLC we build the open→close ('intraday')
leg, measure its **lag-1 autocorrelation** (a mean-reversion gauge) pre- vs post-2022, and
attach a one-shot nearest-expiry **option-chain snapshot** as the only direct 0DTE evidence
yfinance gives. Offline & deterministic apart from the one-time cache fetch; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily SPY **OHLC** (public, no key), 2010-01-05 → 2026-06-18 (**4,139** days, **16.4** years) |
| 0DTE snapshot | yfinance SPY nearest-expiry option chain, **as-of 2026-06-22** (a true 0DTE expiry: 2026-06-22), 32 listed expiries |
| Intraday proxy | open→close log return per day — a **PROXY** for the intraday tape (a daily feed cannot see intraday microstructure) |
| Mean-reversion gauge | lag-1 autocorrelation of the intraday leg; *more negative ⇒ more mean-reverting / more pinned* |
| Structural break | 2022-01-01 (same-day options rolled out Mon/Wed/Fri through 2022) |
| Entry / costs | 1-day execution lag on the naive pin trade; 1 bp one-way cost × turnover |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The 0DTE story is about **intraday**
> microstructure — gamma-hedging into the close — which a **daily** OHLC feed literally
> cannot observe. The open→close lag-1 autocorrelation is the closest daily stand-in for
> "does the tape mean-revert," labelled a proxy throughout. The verdict does **not** claim to
> measure the intraday phenomenon; it shows that on the *measurable* daily proxy the
> cross-2022 change is small and statistically indistinguishable from a random split — and
> that the engine *would* detect a real regime switch if one were there (synthetic control).

## The signal — does the intraday leg get more mean-reverting after 2022?

Lag-1 autocorrelation of the open→close leg, split at 2022. The Welch *t* uses
**block-bootstrap** standard errors (20-day blocks) so serial structure is respected; the
placebo *p* is the share of 5,000 random break dates whose |Δ autocorr| is as large as 2022's.

| leg (proxy) | n pre | n post | autocorr pre | autocorr post | Δ autocorr | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **intraday (open→close)** | 3,020 | 1,119 | **−0.077** | **−0.100** | **−0.023** | **−0.28** | 0.395 |
| close-to-close (control) | 3,020 | 1,119 | −0.130 | −0.027 | **+0.103** | +1.52 | — |

Read it carefully. The intraday leg *did* get slightly **more** negative-autocorrelated post-2022
(−0.077 → −0.100) — the **direction** the 0DTE story predicts. But the change is tiny, at
**t = −0.28 / placebo p = 0.40** it is **statistically indistinguishable from a random split**
of the same tape, and — fatally — the **close-to-close** return moves the **opposite** way
(Δ = **+0.10**, i.e. *less* mean-reverting). A "pinning" effect that shows up in one daily
proxy and reverses in the other is not a robust signal; it is noise wearing the costume of the
narrative.

## Robustness — the effect grows only as you fish the break date later

| assumed break | n post | Δ autocorr | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2021-01-01 | 1,371 | −0.018 | −0.24 |
| **2022-01-01** (rollout) | 1,119 | −0.023 | −0.28 |
| 2022-05-01 | 1,037 | −0.056 | −0.60 |
| 2023-01-01 | 868 | −0.095 | −0.79 |

The |Δ| and |*t*| *increase* the **later** you place the break — the signature of selecting on
a shrinking, more-recent (and more volatile) post-window, not of a clean structural shift. At
no break date does the test approach **t = 2**.

## Can you trade the "pin"? — fade the prior intraday move

Naive contrarian: each day take position **−sign(yesterday's open→close leg)**, entered with a
**1-day lag**, 1 bp one-way cost × turnover. If the tape is *more* pinned post-2022 this should
pay *more* after 2022.

| segment | n days | gross (bp/day) | net @1bp (bp/day) | win-rate | net Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| full sample | 4,139 | +2.17 | +1.16 | 50.0% | 0.23 |
| pre-2022 | 3,020 | +2.62 | +1.61 | 50.0% | 0.33 |
| **post-2022** | 1,119 | +0.95 | **−0.05** | 49.9% | **−0.01** |

The opposite of the claim. The fade trade is **weaker** post-2022, and **net of a single basis
point it loses money** (−0.05 bp/day, Sharpe ≈ 0). Whatever faint mean-reversion the daily proxy
carries, it is *smaller* after the 0DTE boom and does not survive trivial costs — there is no
deployable "trade the pin" edge on the daily tape.

## The 0DTE boom itself is real — the chain snapshot proves it

The boom is not in doubt; only its *measurable daily-tape effect* is. The nearest-expiry SPY
chain **as-of 2026-06-22** (itself a 0DTE expiry, spot ≈ $745) shows the flow:

| metric (current snapshot) | value |
|---|--:|
| total contract volume on the 0DTE expiry | **6.81 M** |
| share of that volume within **±1%** of spot | **89.8%** |
| listed near-daily expiries | **32** (next 8 are consecutive days) |

Nearly **90%** of same-day option volume sits within ±1% of the spot price, across a calendar of
**daily** expiries — that is exactly the at-the-money, same-day gamma wall the pinning story
invokes. The 0DTE *product* is enormous and real; what the daily tape can't confirm is that it
has **pinned** the index.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine detects a real pin, and invents none

A deterministic intraday series with a **pinning regime switch** at the midpoint: after the
switch the intraday leg becomes AR(1) with coefficient **−pin** (more pin ⇒ more mean-reverting).

| planted pin | autocorr pre | autocorr post | Δ autocorr | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no regime change) | +0.003 | +0.023 | +0.020 | **0.68** | 0.149 |
| **0.30** (strong pin) | +0.003 | −0.276 | **−0.279** | **−9.22** | 0.057 |

With **no** planted regime change the test stays at **t = 0.68** (no false break); a **strong
pin** drives **t = −9.2** and the placebo into the tail. The control proves two things at once:
the measurement engine is faithful (it lights up only on a real switch), **and** the real-tape
*t* of **−0.28** is exactly what *no measurable regime change* looks like through this lens.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The intraday-leg autocorrelation does move in the predicted direction
  (−0.077 → −0.100), but the change is small, **fails t ≥ 2** (t = −0.28, placebo p = 0.40),
  **reverses sign** in the close-to-close proxy (+0.10), and grows only as the break date is
  fished later. Proxy-only, direction-consistent-but-insignificant ⇒ **WEAK**, never REAL —
  and a daily feed cannot measure the intraday object the claim is really about.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The naive pin trade is *weaker* post-2022 and **loses money net of
  1 bp** (Sharpe ≈ 0). There is no positive, cost-surviving, post-boom edge to allocate to on
  the daily tape; the tradable version of the claim is absent.
- **"Tape pinned by 0DTE"? — UNPROVEN.** The 0DTE *boom* is unmistakable (≈90% of a 6.8 M-volume
  same-day chain sits at-the-money, on a daily-expiry calendar). But on every daily proxy we can
  build, the claim that it **pinned** the index is statistically indistinguishable from a random
  split — and the honest blocker is that the intraday phenomenon is **not measurable from daily
  data at all**. Real product, unproven tape effect.
